what_changed:
Portal now has clearer top-level sections (Appointments, Care
instructions, Forms and records, Payment method). Email <studio>
button moved to the header. Care instructions render open by
default. "Signed forms" renamed to "Completed forms" with quiet
record styling. PR #158 card-authorization guidance preserved.
why_chloe_should_care:
Clients should feel less lost in the portal. Chloe's smoke-test
feedback drove this restructure.
test_steps:
- Log into the portal as a test client.
- Confirm the "Email Willow" button appears in the header near Sign out.
- Confirm the four top-level sections render with h2 headings.
- Confirm Care instructions are open by default.
- Confirm Completed forms render as a quiet divider list, not as bordered cards.
- Confirm the bottom "Need help?" section is gone.
expected_result:
Portal feels clearer and less cluttered. Contact action is
immediately visible.

what_changed:
Portal renders four explicit card states (no template
configured / authorization needed / signed but no card / active
card). The "Card authorization needed" placeholder explains
exactly what the client must do, with a "Review card
authorization" deep-link to the unsigned-forms section. The
matching practitioner card on the client profile renders the
same four branches with practitioner-actionable copy.
why_chloe_should_care:
Chloe's feedback: "I don't know how to add a card. It should
give you instructions." This PR makes the gating legible to
both the client and the practitioner.
test_steps:
- Open the portal as a client whose studio has an active card_authorization template AND who has NOT yet signed it.
- Expect the "Card authorization needed before adding a card" placeholder.
- Click "Review card authorization" and confirm the page scrolls to the "Review and sign forms" block.
- Sign the card authorization.
- Confirm the Add card form appears with the "You have signed card authorization. You can now add a card on file." line.
- Open the same client's profile as the practitioner.
- Confirm the "Card authorization signed, but no card is on file yet." block renders before the card is added.
expected_result:
Both the client and Chloe always know what to do next, with no
silent gating.

what_changed:
Client profile Sessions tab leads with an Appointments timeline
grouped into Upcoming / Needs charting / Charted / Cancelled /
No-show. Each row exposes the right per-bucket affordance
(Open appointment / Chart session / View session).
why_chloe_should_care:
Chloe asked to see appointment history from the client profile
without context-switching to the calendar.
test_steps:
- Open a client profile with at least one appointment in each status group.
- Switch to the Sessions tab.
- Verify Upcoming shows future confirmed appointments.
- Verify Needs charting offers Chart session linking to /sessions/new?appointment_id=APPT_ID.
- Verify Charted offers View session linking to the linked session detail page.
- Verify Cancelled rows show cancelled_at and cancellation_reason when present and offer no Chart session.
expected_result: Chloe can plan and review without leaving the client profile.

what_changed:
sessions.appointment_id FK added (migration 0068). The calendar
appointment detail page exposes a Chart session button that
stamps the FK on the new session row. startSessionAction
validates studio/client/practitioner lineage before writing the
FK. Historical sessions remain null.
why_chloe_should_care:
Treatment memory now ties each session to a real booking.
Future analytics, billing, and post-care logic depend on this
link being correct.
test_steps:
- Open a future confirmed appointment in the calendar.
- Click "+ Chart session" and confirm the new-session page says it is linking to the appointment.
- Pick a modality and save the session.
- Refresh the appointment detail and confirm it shows View session.
- From a client profile, click "+ Log session" (no appointment context) and confirm the new session has appointment_id null.
expected_result:
Appointment-context flow stamps appointment_id; legacy and
client-scoped flows still work and leave it null.

what_changed:
Every client-facing email (confirmation, reminder, cancellation,
practitioner notification, postcare) now renders appointment
times in 12-hour AM/PM format. Previously a 24-hour body
produced "11:00 to 12:00" / "11:00 - 12:00" which a recipient
on mobile read as "11 to 12".
why_chloe_should_care:
Chloe's recipient sees "11:00 AM to 12:00 PM" now. Less risk
that a client misreads the appointment time and shows up at
the wrong hour.
test_steps:
- Book an 11:00-12:00 appointment for a test client.
- Confirm the confirmation email body reads "11:00 AM to 12:00 PM".
- [object Object]
- Cancel the appointment and confirm the cancellation email uses "at 11:00 AM".
expected_result:
No 24-hour formats anywhere in client-facing email bodies or
subjects.

what_changed:
The Replace card surface no longer requires two clicks. The
autoStart prop with a useRef guard opens the secure card form
immediately when the client lands on the Replace surface from
the portal.
why_chloe_should_care:
A two-click replace was confusing during the smoke test. The
new flow is one obvious action.
test_steps:
- Open the portal as a client with an active card on file.
- Tap Replace card.
- The secure card form should open immediately without a second tap.
- Save a new test card.
- Confirm the read-only summary now shows the new card.
expected_result: One tap from Replace card to the saved-new-card summary.

what_changed:
Photo consent was a single-button "Sign" flow. It is now an
explicit binary. The portal records "granted" or "denied" so
the studio honors the client's actual choice.
why_chloe_should_care:
A client who tapped Sign without reading would have been
consenting silently. Now the choice is explicit on the record.
test_steps:
- Open the portal as a client who has not yet signed photo consent.
- Choose Deny and confirm the Completed forms section shows "Consent denied".
- In another test client, choose Grant and confirm Completed forms shows "Consent granted".
- Verify the client profile in the practitioner view reflects the same response.
expected_result: Both responses are visible and unambiguous on both sides.

what_changed:
SMS confirmation/reminder pipeline (Twilio v1) runs the claim-
then-send-then-record discipline. PR #155 enriched failure
alerts with studio_id. Behavior itself is unchanged.
why_chloe_should_care:
Studio toggles control whether SMS sends. Chloe should verify
that a real client with sms_consent_at on file receives the
confirmation and reminder texts when toggles are on, and
nothing when toggles are off or opt-out is set.
test_steps:
- Book a test appointment for a client with sms_consent_at and a valid phone number, and the studio toggle on for confirmation.
- Confirm the client receives a confirmation SMS within ~15s.
- Toggle the 24h reminder toggle off; do not expect a 24h reminder.
- Toggle it back on and verify the next 24h cron pass sends the reminder.
- Mark the client opted-out and confirm no further SMS sends.
expected_result: SMS only goes to consenting clients with toggles on.

what_changed:
Manual fee charge is test-mode only (PR #146). One
paymentIntents.create call site exists at
lib/billing/manual-fee-charge.ts; everything else is gated.
The duplicate-charge smoke is the load-bearing safety check:
a second click on a charged attempt must NOT produce a second
PaymentIntent.
why_chloe_should_care:
Without this guard a tired practitioner could double-bill a
cancelled client. The whole live-payment posture rests on
this attempt model working correctly even in test mode.
test_steps:
- Find a cancelled or no-show appointment for a client with an active card on file and signed card authorization.
- Use Prepare fee charge to claim a manual fee attempt.
- Click Charge once. Verify the PaymentIntent succeeds in test mode.
- Click Charge again immediately. Verify the second click does NOT create a second PaymentIntent and the UI surfaces the "already attempted" branch.
- Confirm the manual_fee_charge_attempts row reflects one successful attempt only.
expected_result:
Exactly one PaymentIntent per attempt; double-click is a
no-op.
